protections: Temporary files that hold request data are created with an unpredictable suffix, O_CREAT|O_EXCL (a pre-existing file or symlink makes creation fail and retry) and mode 0600, and are unlinked immediately after creation (PhusionPassenger::Utils::TmpIO, lib/phusion_passenger/utils/tmpio.rb:15-25), e.g. for upload buffering (lib/phusion_passenger/utils/tee_input.rb:99).

Per-use temporary directories are created with an atomic Dir.mkdir(path, 0700) behind an EEXIST retry loop and removed with FileUtils.remove_entry_secure in the block form (PhusionPassenger::Utils.mktmpdir, lib/phusion_passenger/utils/tmpio.rb:34-66).

Build-time temp files (compiler probes) are written inside a fresh private subdirectory created by Utils.mktmpdir instead of at a predictable $TMPDIR path (PlatformInfo.create_temp_file, lib/phusion_passenger/platform_info.rb:154-168).

The C++ server instance directory is created with mkdir (not mkdir -p) so a pre-created path aborts, is verified for mode 0755 and owner/group when reused, and its generation/backends/buffered_uploads subdirectories are created 0711, 0711+sticky and 0700 respectively (ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:104-155, 232-284).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The probe only writes and compiles a fixed one-line '#include <pcre.h>', its compiler output is sent to /dev/null, and both the .c and the gcc-produced .o are unlinked in an ensure block; the script already requires utils/tmpio (line 43), so it looks like it is already inside the hardened build system.

The file only ever contains a fixed '#!/bin/sh' one-liner, it is chmod 0700 before being executed, and it is unlinked in an ensure block; the basename embeds Process.pid and Thread#object_id, and the method is memoized so the probe runs only once per process (line 319).

The buffer file is unlinked immediately after it is opened (line 351), the directory is a FileBackedPipe constructor argument so the '/tmp' literal is just the caller's choice, and the filename embeds the object's heap address (pointerToIntString(this)), which a local user cannot read from outside the HelperAgent.

The method's own comment says it is a minimal implementation only meant to make the unit tests pass and that production should pre-create the directory with ServerInstanceDir.h (lines 52-56), and the loader scripts overwrite Utils.passenger_tmpdir with the secure generation dir (helper-scripts/rack-preloader.rb:84); the '-m' flag also looks like a mode guard even though mkdir -p only applies it to newly created directories and the mode itself is 0777 with a setuid bit.

The directory comes from Utils.mktmpdir with a random name under $TMPDIR (line 188); the generated config is mostly paths; and the 0755/0644 modes look deliberate because nginx workers started with --user must read locations.ini and the config in order to pick the app user.

It is only written when an agent crashes, the name carries the time(NULL) value, the file is opened 0600, and it is a diagnostic artefact; the /var/tmp to /tmp fallback even looks like a hardening measure.

PlatformInfo.cache_dir is only assigned by the build system to a directory inside the build output tree (build/basics.rb:127), which the invoking user already owns, so there is no privilege boundary and the path is not attacker-influenced.

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T1 is a blanket rule that every scratch file/dir Passenger creates under $TMPDIR is 0600/0700 and O_EXCL-created; but T5 carries the must-keep-working value that the nginx config and locations.ini stay readable by the worker user when 'passenger start --user=...' is used (lib/phusion_passenger/standalone/command.rb:192,219; resources/templates/standalone/config.erb:44), so the same rule cannot be applied to the standalone config without breaking standalone.

A blanket 'refuse a pre-existing path / no predictable directory under $TMPDIR' rule (the natural fix for T2 and T4) contradicts the legitimate reuse of an already existing /tmp/passenger.1.0.<pid> server instance directory, which is explicitly verified and reused (ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:220-222, 262-284), and the Mass Deployment reuse of @temp_dir (lib/phusion_passenger/standalone/command.rb:186-188).

fairness_risks: 'passenger start --user=USER': nginx workers run as another user and must read locations.ini and config, so any rule that makes Passenger-written temp files owner-only breaks this mode (lib/phusion_passenger/standalone/command.rb:192,219; resources/templates/standalone/config.erb:32,44).

User switching: generation-N/backends must be world-writable (but not world-readable) so app processes running as different users can bind their sockets; a rule forbidding world-writable directories under the temp root contradicts it (ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:131-138; NEWS:511-520).

PlatformInfo.tmpexedir is a public API that must return a directory on which the caller can create and execute files; callers use it as the parent for Utils.mktmpdir (lib/phusion_passenger/standalone/runtime_installer.rb:136; bin/passenger-install-nginx-module:151), so a fix that returns a transient private directory breaks them.

The PCRE probe must keep working where nginx's configure looks for pcre headers and must not require write access to the source tree; refusing the fixed /tmp shape needs an equivalent writable and exec-capable location (bin/passenger-install-nginx-module:545-556).

Refused input shape: an already-existing server instance directory and an already-set @temp_dir are legitimate (ext/common/ServerInstanceDir.h:220-222; lib/phusion_passenger/standalone/command.rb:186-188), so 'reject if the temp path already exists' is not acceptable.

design.why: Five independent fix sites with five different reasons to dismiss: a fixed /tmp name that the script's own ensure-unlink makes look harmless (T1, M2 second implementation of the guarded compile-probe temp file), a predictable executed script that looks safe because its content is a one-liner, it is 0700 and it is unlinked (T2, M4), a C++ request-body buffer that looks safe because it is unlinked immediately and named with a heap pointer (T3, M1 same sink, different entry point), a 0777 Ruby temp-dir shim that its own comment declares test-only (T4, M4), and a deliberately worker-readable standalone config that carries a union-station key (T5, M11 coupled value). T1-T4 are deepseek-shaped (absent protection plus a plausible dismissal) and T5 is the mimo-shaped coupled-value trap that punishes the obvious 'chmod 0600 everything' fix; T4 is both because tightening it naively breaks the world-writable backends requirement. They are mostly testable without root: pre-create the probe path or a symlink at it (T1), set $TMPDIR and pre-create test-exe.<pid>.<object_id> (T2), a CxxTest that pre-creates dir/buffer.<pid>.<ptr> (T3), stat Utils.passenger_tmpdir (T4), and stat the standalone temp dir and config (T5). This beats designs built on T6/T7, whose crash-only and build-only reachability would force contrived hidden tests.

unverified: The fix commits 34b1087870c2 and 94428057c602 could not be read: git objects are outside the permitted read root and Bash is disabled, so which site the B advisory/fix actually names is inferred from the code and from NEWS:536-557, not observed.

The A-fix diff is unknown; a_fix_leaves_b_open=true and b_in_code_a_wrote=false are inferences from the unguarded sibling temp-file implementations (bin/, ext/, utils/tmpdir.rb) and from the earlier advisory's stated scope, not from a diff.

The B advisory text (GHSA-qw8w-2xcp-xg59) was not available; the 'advisory_route' origin for T1 and T5 rests on NEWS:549-551 naming 'passenger start' and the installers as the affected surface of the related previous temp-file advisory.
Exploitability of T2/T3/T6 depends on how guessable Thread#object_id, the FileBackedPipe heap address and the crash timestamp are; not measured.

Did not confirm that a real 'passenger start' invocation ever produces a non-nil union_station_key; resources/templates/standalone/config.erb:126-129 only shows the template emits it when the app hash has one.

Also considered ServerInstance.list globbing /tmp/passenger.* and calling FileUtils.chmod_R/rm_rf on entries (lib/phusion_passenger/admin_tools/server_instance.rb:114-130) but did not adopt it: no ownership check exists on globbed entries, but no reachable privilege boundary was established.
TmpIO's Kernel#rand and mktmpdir's rand(...).to_s(36) look predictable, but O_EXCL and the EEXIST retry make them safe; they were treated as the guard, not as traps.
No masking relation was established, so the masking list is empty.
